natalie (People Ops): Heads up 1 an IC asked if taking a hardship distribution to cover spouse medical bills affects 401(k) rollover options later and whether employer match/vesting changes. tagging @paul and @priya for vendor/process details :wave:
paul (Payroll): Short: hardship is a distribution so it reduces account balance and is taxable (maybe 10% penalty if <59½). Rollover options later depend on whether the distribution was direct rollover-eligible (usually not). Payroll mostly needs the vendor confirmation email to code taxes.
priya (Benefits Admin): Our vendor (HarborRetire) treats hardship as an in-plan distribution, not a direct rollover to another plan. Key points:
- Hardship distribution: taxable; documentation may be required; can't be rolled over if distributed to the participant (unless repaid under very specific rules).
- Loans vs hardship: loans can be repaid and left in plan (so rollover later unaffected). hardship reduces balance permanently and can limit future loan amounts.
- Vesting: employer contributions already vested per schedule. Taking a distribution doesn't clawback vested amounts, but it lowers your balance which may lower maximum loan amounts.
dom: If i take hardship now, can i later roll over remaining balance to an IRA when i leave the company?
priya (Benefits Admin): Yes, any remaining balance that is distributable on termination can be rolled over as usual (subject to plan rules). The hardship amount already taken won't be rolled. Also note: small distributions (<$5k) may be auto-cashed and treated differently.
paul (Payroll): Process/ops checklist for folks:
1) Employee initiates hardship request via Harbor portal: https://portal.harbor.example (choose "Hardship Distribution") and attach supporting docs if asked.
2) Harbor sends confirmation with transaction ID and tax withholding guidance. Employee must forward that to payroll@redwood.example before payroll cutoff.
3) Payroll codes: `HARB_401K_DIST` for taxable distribution, `HARB_401K_WHT` for withholding. Include transaction ID in the ticket.
4) If employee later requests rollover on termination, Harbor will issue distribution paperwork referencing remaining balance.
priya (Benefits Admin): Additional flags:
- If employee is planning a rollover soon, consider waiting to take a hardship since the distribution itself will be taxable and reduce rollover amount.
- Loans outstanding at termination may be offset or treated as distribution per Harbor rules.
- Hardship distributions are final; you can't re-contribute that amount beyond normal deferrals except via standard contributions.
